stem.text: Consider the curve \( y^{2} = 2x^{2}(x + 6) \). There are exactly two points on this curve at which the tangent line is horizontal. Find the \( y \)-coordinate of the one at which \( \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} < 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate implicitly: \( 2y\frac{dy}{dx} = 6 x^{2} + 24 x \), so \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{6 x^{2} + 24 x}{2y} \). The numerator is 0 at \( x = 0 \) and at \( x = -4 \). At \( x = 0 \) the curve gives \( y = 0 \), where the denominator is also 0, so there is no horizontal tangent there. At \( x = -4 \), \( y^{2} = 64 \), so \( y = \pm 8 \) and the denominator is not 0.
Differentiate again, keeping \( y \) as a function of \( x \): \( 2\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2} + 2y\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 12 x + 24 \).
At both points \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 0 \) and \( x = -4 \), so \( \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{-24}{2y} \). At \( y = 8 \) this is \( - \frac{3}{2} \), and at \( y = -8 \) it is \( \frac{3}{2} \).
The second derivative is negative at \( (-4, 8) \), so the \( y \)-coordinate is \( 8 \).

parameter_draw.task: horizontal tangent point selected by the sign of the second derivative
